_metadata.description: Equal capability across the UI, the interactive CLI, the non-interactive CLI, and the API, with one shared session model behind all four.

requirements.title: The wizard shall be completable through the UI, an interactive CLI, and a non-interactive CLI or API call.
requirements.description: Compositional claim for the parity domain. Today the CLI can only submit a hand-authored state document, so headless onboarding, and therefore remote and VPS onboarding, has no usable surface.

validation.notes: The interactive, declarative, and API-backed wizard tests pass; the broad UI readiness gate remains an independent scenario-health limitation.

requirements.title: The CLI shall walk the same steps as the UI in an interactive terminal session.
requirements.description: Same steps, same order, same derived consequences, same locked system set. The terminal presentation differs; the decisions do not.

validation.notes: Interactive wizard tests cover the declared step sequence and resume behavior.

requirements.title: The CLI shall accept a declarative selection document and shall complete setup with no prompt.
requirements.description: The selection document names capabilities the operator wants, not the full internal state shape. It is the surface bridge, cloud, and CI automation drive, and it is what makes remote onboarding possible.

validation.notes: Declarative commit/export tests cover selection translation and no-prompt behavior.

requirements.title: When the same choices are made through the UI, the interactive CLI, and the non-interactive CLI, the resulting operator state shall be identical.
requirements.description: This is the falsifiable form of the parity claim, and the only one that stays true as surfaces evolve. It holds because all three write through one service, not because three code paths were kept in step by review.

validation.notes: The parity regression compares canonical operator-state documents through the shared authority.

requirements.title: When a setup session is started on one surface, another surface shall be able to resume it at the same step.
requirements.description: An operator who starts in the browser and finishes in a terminal, or an agent that takes over a half-finished session, both need the step pointer to be shared state rather than browser memory.

validation.notes: Session tests cover first-unsatisfied-step selection and stable step identity; CLI wizard tests cover the surface resume path.

requirements.title: If the CLI provisions a credential, then it shall read the value from standard input and shall not accept it as a command argument.
requirements.description: A value in argv is visible in the process table and in shell history. Standard input is the only accepted channel, and the command rejects a value-bearing flag rather than warning about it.

validation.notes: Credential tests reject value-bearing flags and exercise standard-input provisioning.

requirements.title: If a required readiness item is not ready, then the readiness command shall exit with a non-zero status.
requirements.description: Automation cannot branch on prose. A machine-readable exit code is what lets bridge, cloud provisioning, and CI gate on a real readiness result.

validation.notes: Readiness tests assert the machine-readable required-blocker exit contract.

requirements.title: A CLI command's declared Connect binding shall name a service and method that exist in the generated descriptors.
requirements.description: The manifest is the CLI surface authority. Connect-bound commands are checked against every generated onboarding service descriptor; local file and workflow exceptions carry an explicit architecture exception and are checked separately.

validation.notes: TestCLIManifestMatchesGeneratedProtoSurface checks every Connect binding, every omission, and every local exception; TestCLIManifestProtoParityHasTeeth proves a nonexistent method fails.

requirements.title: Every onboarding HTTP route that is not a Connect procedure shall carry one of the canonical REST exception reasons.
requirements.description: The onboarding API has only the health probe exceptions. The transport drift gate checks both UI HTTP calls and direct main.go route registrations against the tagged exception set.
